sheet-2.description: Sheet 2 covers a residential district in the north-western part of Englewood, drawn at 50 feet to an inch and turned so that north lies towards the upper left. West Demarest Avenue crosses the top left of the sheet, Knickerbocker Road runs down the western side from it to the bottom edge, and West Palisade Avenue closes the sheet along the bottom. Liberty Road crosses diagonally from Knickerbocker Road towards the east, and Central Avenue and West End Avenue meet on the right-hand side, where the sheet continues on sheet 3. Otsego Place and Cottage Place are short streets marked mainly by water pipes. The West Side Presbyterian Church with its parish house, drawn in blue as a brick or cinder block building, stands on the south side of West Demarest Avenue near the north-west corner. Elsewhere the blocks are divided into long, narrow lots with detached frame dwellings, drawn in yellow, some with auto houses, and a few buildings with brick or tile walls in pink. A row of small buildings in blue stands in the lower middle of the sheet. Six-inch water pipes with hydrants run in most streets, and a 24-inch main crosses Knickerbocker Road and Liberty Road near their junction. Block numbers 97, 99 and 100 and the numbers of the neighbouring sheets (18, 37, 3, 6 and 7) are printed on the sheet. A large part of the western edge, west of Knickerbocker Road, is blank, belonging to sheet 37.
notes: Otsego Place, Cottage Place and Brookway Avenue exist in OpenStreetMap under the same names; their junctions with the streets listed were not used as control.
West Side Presbyterian Church and its parish house stand on the south side of West Demarest Avenue.
50 ft. West Demarest Av, Knickerbocker Rd, Liberty Rd, Central Av, West End Av, West Palisade Av; church top left.

sheet-3.description: Sheet 3 covers a mixed residential and commercial district in the north-western part of Englewood, at 50 feet to an inch, with north towards the upper left. Tenafly Road runs down the left-centre of the sheet. West End Avenue and Liberty Road join it from the west, while Henry, Grove and Charles streets run east from it to James Street, which forms the right-hand side of the sheet. West Palisade Avenue crosses the bottom. Most blocks are lined with detached frame dwellings with auto houses, drawn in yellow, with a few brick or tile buildings in pink and cinder block auto buildings in blue. St. John's Evangelical Lutheran Church stands on the west side of Tenafly Road, and Liberty School, a large pink brick building with its playground, occupies the lower left. The Garden Arms Apartments stand on the block between Henry and Grove streets, and large greenhouses fill the block east of Tenafly Road below Grove Street. Along West Palisade Avenue the lower right of the sheet is built up with a continuous row of brick stores, a hotel, auto showrooms, an auto radiator repair shop, a bus garage and an auto storage garage. Six-inch and 24-inch water pipes run in most streets. Block numbers 99 to 105 and the numbers of the neighbouring sheets (2, 18, 19, 4, 7 and 8) are printed on the sheet. Part of the lower margin carries the scale bar and the Sanborn copyright line.
notes: Henry, Grove, Charles and James are printed without a suffix; today they are Henry Street, Grove Street, Charles Street and James Street.
Tallman Place, Armory Street, Lafayette Avenue and Bennett Road were not used as control.
Liberty School, St. John's Evangelical Lutheran Church and the Garden Arms Apartments are named on the sheet.
50 ft. Tenafly Rd, Henry, Grove, Charles, James, West Palisade Av; Liberty School.

sheet-4.description: Sheet 4 shows the north-west side of central Englewood, drawn at 50 feet to an inch and turned so that north points to the upper left. West Palisade Avenue runs across the bottom of the sheet and James Street along the left edge. West Street, a narrow street lettered only West, slants down from Tallman Place to Palisade Avenue and divides the sheet into a western and an eastern half. Tallman Place crosses the upper part of the sheet, and a short extension of it, lettered Tallman Place Square, runs down between blocks 105 and 107. At the right the sheet reaches N. Van Brunt Street, also lettered Depot Sq. W., and the Northern Railroad of New Jersey (Erie) tracks, with the railroad station and a freight building near the top right. Overpeck Creek crosses the middle of the sheet from the upper centre to Palisade Avenue, spanned by a small bridge near a hand laundry. The western half is mainly frame dwellings on narrow lots along James Street, with a builder's yard and lumber shed at the top. Along West Palisade Avenue the sheet shows a continuous row of stores of one and two storeys, a feed warehouse, a cinder-block garage and a larger garage. On the east side of West Street stand the Plaza Theatre, a garage with a cinder-block annex, a trucking and storage building, a stone-cutting works, the American Legion Hall and the Municipal Building, a fire-proof building. The blocks are numbered 105 to 109. The top of the sheet carries the label Englewood N.J. and the date January 1929, and the lower edge a scale bar and the Princeton University Library stamp.
notes: West, the slanting street lettered West, is Nathaniel Place in OpenStreetMap; it meets Tallman Place and West Palisade Avenue.
North Van Brunt Street is drawn about 52 feet wide with the Erie tracks along its east side; its junctions were not detected and it was used only as a check.
Georeferenced from four junctions on the west half of the sheet (James, Tallman Place, West and West Palisade Avenue); the east end rests on the fitted scale and rotation.
50 ft. James St, Tallman Pl, West (Nathaniel Place), West Palisade Av, N. Van Brunt St and the Erie station; Overpeck Creek; Plaza Theatre, Municipal Building.

sheet-5-1.description: Part 1 of sheet 5 is the main map of Englewood's business district, drawn at 50 feet to an inch and turned so that north points to the upper left. Palisade Avenue runs across the bottom edge, N. Dean Street runs up the left-centre of the sheet from Palisade Avenue to Park Place, and Engle Street runs up the right-centre. Bergen Street crosses from N. Dean to Engle in the lower half. The Northern Railroad of New Jersey (Erie) tracks and N. Van Brunt Street occupy the left edge, with Depot Place crossing them near the middle. The lower blocks, numbered 110 and 113, are densely built with one- and two-storey brick stores along Palisade Avenue, among them drug stores, a public service substation, an electric substation, the Englewood Press and an ice cream works. Along N. Dean Street are garages, a repair shop, lumber and wagon sheds and a printing works. The upper blocks, 112 and part of 25, hold dwellings, the Armory with a cinder-block garage beside it, an auto show room and the New Jersey Bell Telephone Company buildingand frame dwellings in the upper blocks. On the left side of N. Dean Street are stores, a cinder-block building, a flour, grain and hay warehouse, a chrome plating works and several warehouses. Park Place crosses the top of the sheet. The part is cut by the heavy line of the box at the upper right, which belongs to part 2. The sheet is dated January 1929.
notes: N. Dean is North Dean Street and Bergen is Bergen Street in OpenStreetMap; the Palisade Avenue of this sheet is East Palisade Avenue.
Georeferenced from five detected junctions (Palisade Avenue, Bergen Street and Park Place with N. Dean and Engle).
50 ft. Two parts: 1 main downtown (Palisade Av, N. Dean, Bergen, Engle, Depot Pl, Park Pl; armory); 2 box upper right drawn out of position (Demarest Av, N. Dean, Engle, Park Pl).

sheet-5-2.description: Part 2 of sheet 5 is the boxed block at the upper right of the sheet, enclosed by a heavy line that runs from the top edge down to the left of the box and along its lower side. It is drawn at 50 feet to an inch and turned so that north points to the upper left, like the main map, but it is placed away from the ground it belongs to, so that Park Place and N. Dean Street appear a second time inside the box. The box shows the area north of Park Place: E. (W.) Demarest Avenue across the top, where the Englewood N.J. label stands, N. Dean Street along the heavy left edge, Engle Street at the right, with Church Street entering Engle Street at the upper right, and Park Place along the bottom. The upper blocks, numbered 20 and 25, are laid out with narrow lots, and the north part is mostly detached frame dwellings of one and two and a half storeys with a few cinder-block garages and stores near N. Dean Street. Along Park Place at the bottom stand larger brick and frame buildings, among them the Palisade Trust and Guarantee Company, the Englewood Mutual Loan and Building Association, and a row of stores. A compass rose and north arrow stand in the lower middle of the box. The sheet is dated January 1929.
notes: Georeferenced from North Dean Street and Park Place as an anchor at 7.85 px/ft, with the other junctions (East Demarest Avenue, Engle Street) detected after the anchor; the part is drawn displaced from the ground it covers.
Church Street is lettered at the right edge of the box.
50 ft. Two parts: 1 main downtown (Palisade Av, N. Dean, Bergen, Engle, Depot Pl, Park Pl; armory); 2 box upper right drawn out of position (Demarest Av, N. Dean, Engle, Park Pl).

sheet-6.description: Sheet 6 covers the west side of Englewood below West Palisade Avenue, drawn at 50 feet to an inch and turned so that north lies towards the upper left. West Palisade Avenue runs along the top edge of the sheet. Brookway Avenue curves down from it through the middle, Cottage Place runs south-east from it along the right side, and Mattlage Place runs down the left side, crossing Shepard Avenue, Howland Avenue and Washington Avenue. West Englewood Avenue, which the sheet also labels Lafayette Avenue, crosses the lower part diagonally from lower left to right, and Park Avenue leaves it on the right. Lafayette Avenue runs south from it at the bottom of the sheet. A brook, drawn in blue, enters near the upper left and runs south-east across the sheet to the middle. The blocks are divided into long narrow lots, nearly all with detached frame dwellings and auto houses. Larger buildings include the National Italian Corporation Club House on the east side of Brookway Avenue, a cement block manufacturing building near the brook, a brick auto repair building west of Brookway Avenue near West Englewood Avenue, the Lafayette Apartments with drugs store at the corner of West Englewood Avenue, and a short row of brick and frame stores at the lower left. The streets carry six-inch water pipes, with hydrants and fire alarm and telephone markers. Block numbers 130, 131 and 132 and the numbers of the adjoining sheets (37, 38, 2, 7 and 31) are printed on the sheet. The bold lines at the left and top edges leave the parts west of Mattlage Place and above West Palisade Avenue blank.
notes: The main diagonal street is labelled Lafayette Avenue or West Englewood Avenue; it is West Englewood Avenue in OpenStreetMap.
Washington Avenue is Washington Place in OpenStreetMap.
Cleveland Street, Mattlage Place and West Palisade Avenue meet at one node in OpenStreetMap at the upper left of the sheet.
Brookway Avenue is drawn about 38 feet wide where the parcels give 60 feet.
Lafayette Place / West Englewood Avenue was not detected and is not used as control.
50 ft. Brookway Av, Cottage Pl, Mattlage Pl, West Englewood Av (also lettered Lafayette Av), brook.

sheet-7-1.description: Sheet 7, part 1 is the main map of the sheet and covers a district in the west of Englewood, at 50 feet to an inch with north towards the upper left. West Palisade Avenue runs along the top of the sheet. Cottage Place runs south-east along the left side, and Salem Place crosses the block east of it. Lafayette Avenue curves from the lower left towards the upper right, ending near West Palisade Avenue, and West Englewood Avenue crosses the lower half from left to right to Bennett Road on the right-hand edge. Park Avenue and Elmore Avenue run south from West Englewood Avenue through the lower blocks. A strip of lots with detached frame dwellings and auto houses fronts West Palisade Avenue, and the West Side Presbyterian Church stands at its east end. Two wedge-shaped blocks lie between Cottage Place and Lafayette Avenue. The large block east of Lafayette Avenue, between the curving avenue and Bennett Road, is mostly open, with a filling station near West Englewood Avenue, and a pink building and open ground beside Lafayette Avenue. South of West Englewood Avenue the blocks hold rows of dwellings, with a few brick buildings drawn in pink near the junction of Lafayette Avenue and Park Avenue. A brook, drawn in blue, and Mackay Park run down the right-hand edge. The Englewood Country Club inset occupies the lower left of the sheet and is a separate part. Block numbers 133 to 137 and the numbers of the neighbouring sheets (2, 3, 6, 8 and 31) are printed on the sheet.
notes: Salem Place appears to be Haring Place in OpenStreetMap (matched by position); the junctions of Haring Place with Cottage Place and Lafayette Avenue were used as control.
The street labelled Lafayette Avenue or Englewood Avenue is West Englewood Avenue in OpenStreetMap.
The lower-left box with the Englewood Country Club is drawn separately and is not part of this annotation.
Elmore Avenue / West Englewood Avenue was left out of the fit: it carried a residual of about 3.5 m.
50 ft. Two parts: 1 main (W. Palisade Av, Cottage Pl, Salem Pl, Lafayette Av, W. Englewood Av, Park Av, Elmore Av, Bennett Rd); 2 boxed inset of the Englewood Country Club, not placed.

Not georeferenced on this sheet: inset: Englewood Country Club (club house, laundry, sleeping quarters) (no street junction or lettered street in the box; ground location not identified; needs identification of the club house site and a parcel-corner or carried point, px_per_ft 7.9, north_deg from its own arrow).

sheet-8.description: Sheet 8 covers the west side of Englewood between West Palisade Avenue at the top and West Englewood Avenue across the middle, drawn at 50 feet to an inch and turned so that north points to the upper left. Bennett Road forms the left side of the built block, Armory Street runs down the middle and William Street forms the right edge. The blocks, numbered 138 and 139, hold a mixture of uses: at the top, auto repairing and show rooms, a vulcanizing shop and a large brick auto showroom; in the middle, rows of one-storey cinder-block garages, a gymnasium and school, a synagogue, a hall of the Social Service Federation (a memorial building) and the Elks Club; and detached frame dwellings on narrow lots along Bennett Road and William Street. Bethany Presbyterian Church (Colored) and the Galilee M.E. Church stand on the east side. Overpeck Creek runs through the sheet from the upper right to the foot and is crossed by West Englewood Avenue. South of West Englewood Avenue the sheet is largely open ground: Mackay Park (block 137) fills the left and centre, with a compass rose, and a few dwellings and stores stand along the east side (block 166). A second branch of the creek runs near the left edge. Lafayette Avenue enters at the upper left. The scale bar is at the lower left, and the sheet is dated January 1929.
notes: Armory is Armory Street in OpenStreetMap and Bennett Road is unchanged.

sheet-9.description: Sheet 9 shows the centre of Englewood south-west of the railroad, drawn at 50 feet to an inch and turned so that north points to the upper left. West Palisade Avenue forms the top and West Englewood Avenue crosses the middle; William, Humphrey and Van Brunt streets run down the sheet. The upper blocks, numbered 140 and 143, hold the commercial core: fire department headquarters, a garage, plumbers' supplies, a mission, Lincoln School with its gymnasium, stores, auto garages, the Salvation Army Mission, a battery service station and the Englewood Hygeia Ice Company with its ice storage and freezing tanks. The Hygeia Hotel stands near West Englewood Avenue. Along the right side the Northern Railroad of New Jersey (Erie) tracks run beside the Englewood Coal and Lumber Company's lumber shed and yard. The lower blocks, numbered 141, 142, 144 and 146, are mostly detached frame dwellings on narrow lots, with a Baptist church (First Baptist) at the left, a bakery, stores, wagon sheds and ruins of a burned building. A street lettered School runs down the left side. Jay Street runs along the bottom, where block 32 is lettered. A compass rose stands near the upper right and the scale bar at the lower right. The sheet is dated January 1929.
notes: William Street was left out of the control: its junction with West Englewood Avenue lay 5 to 6 m from the line of the other four junctions.
Van Brunt is South Van Brunt Street in OpenStreetMap.
50 ft. Downtown west of the Erie: West Palisade Av, William, Humphrey, Van Brunt, West Englewood Av, Jay.

sheet-10.description: Sheet 10 covers the south-east side of Englewood's business centre, east of the railroad, drawn at 50 feet to an inch and turned so that north points to the upper left. Palisade Avenue runs across the top and E. Englewood Avenue across the middle, with S. Dean Street running down the sheet from the upper left to the lower right and Grand Avenue along the right edge. At the top, block 5 holds a row of one- and two-storey stores along Palisade Avenue including the Englewood Theatre, a hay and feed storage warehouse, garages and an auto show room, with the New Jersey Bell Telephone Company's auto show rooms on the right. To the left of S. Dean Street are the tracks of the Northern Railroad of New Jersey (Erie) and the yard of the Englewood Coal and Lumber Company, with coal sheds and coal pockets, the Tuttle Bros. lumber yard and the Standard Oil Company's tanks at the bottom. The right side, blocks 149, 150A and 11, is mainly frame dwellings with a garage, stone works and the storage warehouses of Markham and Sons and the Palisade Storage Warehouse Company. A compass rose stands at the left and the scale bar at the lower left. Tracy Place and Grand Avenue meet at the right edge. The sheet is dated January 1929.
notes: E. Englewood Avenue east of S. Dean Street is West Englewood Avenue in OpenStreetMap; Tracy Place is Tracey Place.
Five junctions are used; fit is 0.7 m RMSE with leave-one-out 1.9 m.

sheet-11.description: Sheet 11 shows the southern end of the Englewood business district east of the Northern Railroad of New Jersey (Erie), drawn at 50 feet to an inch and turned so that north points to the upper left. S. Dean Street runs down the sheet from top to bottom, with Grand Avenue curving down the right side. Garrett Place crosses the middle between them, Chester Place enters Grand Avenue near the top, and Franklin Avenue enters it below Garrett Place. Linden Avenue runs along the bottom edge. The railroad and its yards run down the left, with a block numbered 171 and 32 on the left holding little more than a long coal pocket structure and the yard of H. P. Cole, coal and wood. The Mountain Ice Company stands at the upper left, with its ice storage, and the Sash, Door and Trim Company of Englewood is at the top. The blocks east of S. Dean Street, numbered 150A and 150B, are largely open ground with scattered detached frame dwellings and a few garages, and an apartment house with an auto show room stands at Garrett Place. At the bottom are Joseph E. Quirk's storage warehouse and a cinder-block fire-proof building, with the lots of Linden Avenue. A compass rose stands at the right and the scale bar at the lower left. The sheet is dated January 1929.
notes: Garrett Place is Garret Place in OpenStreetMap; Franklin Avenue is Franklin Street and Linden Avenue is East Linden Avenue.
Three of the five points are hand-picked (Chester Place, Franklin Street and East Linden Avenue); S. Dean Street is drawn on a curve, so the fit is medium to low confidence.
50 ft. S. Dean, Garrett Pl, Grand Av, Chester Pl, Franklin Av, Linden Av; Quirk storage warehouse.

sheet-12.description: Sheet 12 covers a residential part of Englewood between Palisade Avenue, which runs along the top edge of the sheet, and the lower end of Dwight Place, drawn at 50 feet to an inch and turned so that north lies towards the upper left. Grand Avenue runs down the left side, bending at the top towards Palisade Avenue, and Dwight Place runs diagonally down the right side. Tracy Place crosses the middle of the sheet from Grand Avenue to Dwight Place, and a short stretch of Englewood Avenue enters Grand Avenue from the left. Lyman Place and Sherwood Place leave Dwight Place at the right edge. The upper block, numbered 151, is dominated by the Dwight Manor Apartments, a large brick-and-tile building of five storeys drawn in pink, with stand-pipe and fire-escape symbols and the note that no hose is provided with the stand pipes. Around it stand frame dwellings with rear auto houses on large lots, and a cinder-block storage building drawn in blue beside the block's southern line. The block below Tracy Place, numbered 152, has smaller lots along Grand Avenue, with a stone dwelling, frame houses and garages, and larger properties towards Dwight Place, including a dwelling drawn with a blue stone or concrete shell. Water pipes of 6 and 24 inches are marked in the streets, with hydrants, fire alarm boxes and telephone-pole symbols. Neighbouring sheet numbers 10, 13, 25, 27 and 30 are printed in the margins, the scale bar sits at the bottom, and a compass rose shows north to the upper left.
notes: Palisade Avenue is East Palisade Avenue in OpenStreetMap.
Tracy Place is Tracey Place in OpenStreetMap.
Englewood Avenue is West Englewood Avenue today.
Dwight Manor Apartments stand in block 151 on Palisade Avenue.

sheet-13.description: Sheet 13 lies directly south of sheet 12 in the Dwight Place district of Englewood and is drawn at 50 feet to an inch, turned so that north lies towards the upper left. Grand Avenue curves down the left side of the sheet and Dwight Place runs down the right side; Chestnut Place, Franklin Avenue and Linden Avenue cross between them from top to bottom, and Garrett Place, Maple Street and Sherwood Place appear as short stubs at the margins. Howard Place is a short dead-end street running south from Chestnut Place, closed at its lower end by a rounded turn-around with a pair of blue-shelled auto houses at the end. The top block, numbered 152, carries only a few large frame dwellings. The block between Chestnut Place and Franklin Avenue, numbered 172, is closely built with frame dwellings and rear auto houses along Howard Place and Franklin Avenue, with a large property in its north-east corner. The block below Franklin Avenue, numbered 173, has a regular row of narrow lots facing Franklin Avenue, each with a two-and-a-half storey frame dwelling, and larger lots with scattered dwellings and garages towards Linden Avenue. Almost all buildings are shown in yellow as frame, with a few brick-veneer and concrete-block outbuildings in pink and blue. Six-inch water pipes run in most streets, and a 24-inch main follows Grand Avenue. House numbers are printed along the street fronts. The adjoining sheets named in the margins are 11, 12, 30 and 33, the scale bar is at lower right, and a compass rose to the right shows north to the upper left.
notes: Chestnut Place is Chester Place in OpenStreetMap; sheet 30 prints it as Chester Pl.
Franklin Avenue is Franklin Street today.
Linden Avenue is East Linden Avenue in OpenStreetMap.
Garrett Place is Garret Place in OpenStreetMap.
50 ft. Chestnut (Chester) Pl, Howard Pl, Franklin Av, Linden Av, Grand Av, Dwight Pl.

sheet-14-1.description: Sheet 14, part 1 is the main map of a sparsely built district in the north-east of Englewood, drawn at 50 feet to an inch. Engle Street runs down the middle of the sheet, a street of about 65 feet with a water pipe along its centre, and Glenwood Road leaves it to the east at the bottom right. West of Engle Street lies the grounds of Englewood Hospital, labelled across its lawns: a cluster of pink and yellow buildings at the top (wards, a laundry building, a maternity ward and a clinic, joined by covered passages), a long brown fireproof main block with an operating room, a nurses home with a long dormitory, a stone building and a small power house, all marked with steam heat, electric light and gas, and linked by dashed pipe lines to hydrants and test holes. Brookside Cemetery borders the grounds along the north edge. At the bottom left, Browne's Terrace and the lots on either side of it hold two rows of small frame dwellings and sheds in block 45. East of Engle Street lie the open grounds of the Englewood Field Club, with a dashed outline of tennis courts. A railroad is lettered along the left edge. Adjoining sheet numbers (16, 17, 24, 25, 37) are printed in the margins. The inset in the top right corner is a separate part.
notes: Engle is Engle Street, and Glenwood Road is unchanged, in OpenStreetMap.
Browne's Terrace is not in the OpenStreetMap extract and was not used for control.
Placed from the Engle Street and Glenwood Road junction alone, with the scale and rotation of its neighbours: low confidence.
The railroad along the left edge is lettered N. R. R. of N. J. (Erie).
50 ft. Two parts: 1 Englewood Hospital grounds, Engle St, Glenwood Rd, Browne's Terrace; 2 inset top right: Englewood Field Club club house (carried from part 1).

sheet-14-2.description: Sheet 14, part 2 is the inset in the top right corner of the sheet, boxed by heavy lines, drawn at 50 feet to an inch. It shows the Club House of the Englewood Field Club, a long yellow frame building of one and two storeys marked with steam heat, lights, electricity and fire extinguishers on a district hydrant, with a rear wing at its east end. The box is the continuation of the main map eastward: a dash-and-dot match line lettered A at the top and B at the bottom cuts the club house at its west end, and the same corner of the building is repeated at the right edge of part 1, where it carries the sheet number 14. A line lettered No Exposure runs across the top of the box, and the number 37 below the building marks the sheet that carries this ground. No streets are shown. The inset shares the orientation of part 1; a compass rose below it points north up and to the left.
notes: Placed only by two points carried from the club house corner repeated on part 1 at the A-B match line, plus the scale and rotation of part 1: low confidence, no street control.
The inset is taken to be at the same scale as part 1 (50 ft to an inch); no scale is printed on the inset itself.
50 ft. Two parts: 1 Englewood Hospital grounds, Engle St, Glenwood Rd, Browne's Terrace; 2 inset top right: Englewood Field Club club house (carried from part 1).

sheet-15.description: Sheet 15 covers a residential district in the north of Englewood between Central Avenue on the west and Tenafly Road on the east, drawn at 50 feet to an inch. Jane crosses the top of the sheet, Slocum Avenue crosses the middle and John runs along the bottom, all slanting down toward Tenafly Road. Central Avenue runs north and south along the left side, and Tenafly Road along the right edge, with Hamilton Avenue shown meeting it at the upper right. The blocks are laid out in long, narrow lots, built up with one- and two-storey frame dwellings with auto houses and sheds. A few commercial and service buildings stand along the south side of the lower block: a carpenter shop, lumber storage, a plumber and an office, and a small blue-tinted dwelling. Chicken houses appear in the back lots of the two northern blocks. A larger dwelling with extensions stands at the bottom right, and a cluster of houses lies in block 49 at the lower left, west of Central Avenue. Water pipes of 4 and 6 inches run in the streets with hydrants and fire alarm boxes. Block numbers 49, 50 and 51 and sheet numbers 16, 18, 22 and 37 are printed on the sheet.
notes: Jane, John and Slocum Avenue are Jane Street, John Street and Slocum Avenue in OpenStreetMap.
50 ft. Central Av to Tenafly Rd, Jane, Slocum Av, John.

sheet-16.description: Sheet 16 covers a residential district in the north-central part of Englewood, between Tenafly Road on the west and Overpeck Creek on the east, drawn at 50 feet to an inch. Brook Avenue crosses the top of the sheet, Hamilton Avenue and Slocum Avenue run across its middle, all three slanting down from Tenafly Road towards the creek. Prospect runs south from Hamilton Avenue through the lower half of the sheet, and Waldo Place runs north and south through the eastern third, curving at its north end into Brook Avenue. West (George) Street edges the sheet in the south-east corner. The blocks are divided into narrow, deep house lots, most built up with one- and two-storey frame dwellings with rear auto houses and sheds; a few stores, a vendor's shop and concrete-block auto houses are scattered among them. The Finnish Bethel Congregational Church stands on the west side of Waldo Place just north of Hamilton Avenue, and a small printing shop sits behind the houses of block 44A east of Waldo Place. The east edge of the district is open ground along Overpeck Creek, drawn in blue, with lots running down to its bank. Water pipes of 6 inches are shown in most streets, with hydrant and fire alarm symbols. Block numbers (44A, 52, 53, 54, 55, 65, 68) and the numbers of adjoining sheets (15, 17, 19, 24, 7) are printed in the margins and blocks. The lots facing Tenafly Road on the west edge belong to the next sheet and are shown only in part.
notes: Hamilton Avenue is West Hamilton Avenue in OpenStreetMap.
West (George) is West Street today.
Finnish Bethel Congregational Church on Waldo Place north of Hamilton Avenue.

sheet-17.description: Sheet 17 covers the area on both sides of the Northern Railroad of New Jersey (Erie) in the north-central part of Englewood, drawn at 50 feet to an inch. The railroad runs north to south through the middle of the sheet as a bundle of parallel tracks. West of it, Overpeck Creek, drawn in blue, winds down the left side. Slocum Avenue crosses the creek and the railroad corridor, Browne and Railroad Avenue run north and south beside the tracks, and West (George) Street edges the sheet on the far left. The blocks west of the tracks are built up with small frame dwellings and some small brick parts, and a building supply yard with a lumber shed and tile storage stands at the lower left. East of the tracks, Hamilton Avenue crosses the sheet diagonally. Along it stand a large concrete garage for 75 cars, and further south a Public Service transformer station with its gas department warehouse, and a garage and repair shop of Stillman and Hoag built in 1927. Large open parcels lie in blocks 45 and 58, with scattered dwellings. Engle runs north and south along the right edge, Chestnut crosses the bottom and Booth Avenue joins at the upper right. Water pipes and fire alarm boxes are shown in the streets.
notes: Hamilton Avenue is West Hamilton Avenue and East Hamilton Avenue in OpenStreetMap; West (George) is West Street.
Browne, Railroad Avenue and Walker Alley are not in the OpenStreetMap extract by those names.

sheet-18-1.description: Part 1 is the main map of sheet 18, drawn at 50 feet to an inch and turned so that north points to the upper left. It covers the north-eastern edge of Englewood along Tenafly Road, which forms the right-hand boundary of the sheet. John Street runs across the top and Morse Place and West Demarest Avenue cut across the middle, so that the sheet is divided into three bands of long residential blocks. Otsego Place runs down the left side between John Street and West Demarest Avenue. The blocks are cut into narrow lots of about 40 to 50 feet, built up with one- and two-storey frame dwellings with small outbuildings, a few of them brick-trimmed; two pink-edged buildings in the top band are brick. The largest building is the Methodist Episcopal Church on West Demarest Avenue near Tenafly Road. Below West Demarest Avenue the streets turn: Central Avenue runs down the left and West End Avenue crosses the lower part on a slant, and the blocks between them are cut into long, tapering lots running back to Tenafly Road. Henry Street is lettered where it enters Tenafly Road at the right edge. Six-inch and eight-inch water pipes and hydrants are marked in the streets. The part is bounded on the lower left by the heavy dividing line of the boxed block (part 2). The Englewood stamp and the January 1929 date stand in the top band; the compass rose is at the bottom, left of Central Avenue.
notes: John Street, Morse Place, West Demarest Avenue, Central Avenue, West End Avenue and Tenafly Road keep their names in OpenStreetMap (John Street, Morse Place and so on); Otsego Place is not in OpenStreetMap as a through street.
Morse Place appears in OpenStreetMap with a junction only at Tenafly Road; the junction was detected from the drawn lines.

Tenafly Road junctions were measured from the drawn edge of the street, since the sheet cuts it at the right-hand margin.

sheet-18-2.description: Part 2 is a boxed block at the lower left of sheet 18, enclosed by a heavy line, drawn at 50 feet to an inch with north to the upper left (an arrow stands at the top of the box). It shows the blocks between John Street at the top and West Demarest Avenue at the bottom, west of the heavy line and along the east side of Knickerbocker Road, which curves down the left side of the box and is marked 60 feet wide. The box is lettered 37 outside it and 18 and 2 inside, marking the continuation on sheet 37 to the west. The lots are deep and mostly unbuilt in the lower half, where a few frame dwellings and outbuildings stand along the street frontages; the upper half has frame dwellings with brick-trimmed outbuildings. Six-inch water pipes run in Knickerbocker Road, John Street and West Demarest Avenue, with a hydrant at the upper left. The block is drawn out of line with part 1, which is cut off by the heavy line, so it was placed on its own.
notes: Placed only from the 6 inch water pipe junctions at John Street / Knickerbocker Road and Knickerbocker Road / West Demarest Avenue, which lie on one street: low confidence, scale fitted 3 percent below the sheet value.
West Demarest Avenue is printed along the bottom edge of the sheet and its centre falls almost on the sheet edge.
50 ft. Two parts: 1 main (John, Morse Pl, Otsego Pl, W. Demarest Av, Central Av, West End Av, Tenafly Rd); 2 lower-left box (John, Knickerbocker Rd, W. Demarest Av).

sheet-19.description: Sheet 19 covers a district in the west of Englewood around West Demarest Avenue, drawn at 50 feet to an inch. Tenafly Road runs north and south along the left edge, Prospect and Waldo Place run north and south across the middle, and West (George) Street runs down the right edge. Division crosses the top, Demot crosses the middle diagonally and West Demarest Avenue runs from the lower left to the lower right. Henry runs along the bottom left and James meets West Demarest Avenue near the bottom. The upper part of the sheet is a mix of house lots and larger holdings: the Lauvir Court Apartments, a cinder block building with two wings, and Sisters House, with open fields around them in blocks 65 and 18. A long row of garages and a row of attached houses stand beside Prospect. St. Cecilia's Roman Catholic complex occupies the central block, with its school, a second school building, the priory and the church with a tower. The Christian Reformed Church and its parsonage hall stand near the lower left. The right-hand strip along Waldo Place and West Street is a row of narrow house lots with dwellings and small outbuildings. Water pipes and hydrants are shown throughout.
notes: Prospect, Division, Demot, Henry and James are Prospect Street, Division Street, Demott Street, Henry Street and James Street in OpenStreetMap.
West (George) is West Street today.
Lauvir Court Apartments, St. Cecilia's R.C. School, Priory and Church, Christian Reformed Church.

sheet-20.description: Sheet 20 covers the area where West Demarest Avenue crosses the Northern Railroad of New Jersey (Erie) and Overpeck Creek, in the west of Englewood, drawn at 50 feet to an inch. West (George) Street runs down the left side and North Dean runs along the east side of the tracks. Overpeck Creek, drawn in blue, curves down from the upper left to the middle of the sheet and passes under West Demarest Avenue. West Demarest Avenue runs across the bottom, changing to East Demarest Avenue on the right of the tracks. The railroad is shown as several parallel tracks running from the top to the bottom. West of the creek lie blocks 70 and 19 with scattered frame dwellings on long lots. Along the tracks are the Public Service Gas Company buildings, a Hackensack Water Company garage and a carpenter shop with an express office. East of the tracks, North Dean and Walker Alley carry a row of dwellings, a warehouse and a ruined building marked ruins of fire. Chestnut crosses the top. At the bottom left, the Building Supply Company of Englewood occupies a lumber yard, and a park is lettered at the bottom between the tracks and North Dean. Waldo Place and James appear at the lower left.
notes: North Dean is North Dean Street today; Walker Alley is Walkers Lane in OpenStreetMap (its junction with Chestnut was hand-picked).
West (George) is West Street; James is James Street.
Only four control points: low to medium confidence.
Public Service Gas Co., Hackensack Water Co., Building Supply Co. of Englewood; the lettered park at the bottom is unnamed.
50 ft, turned about -35 degrees. W. Demarest Av across the Erie tracks and Overpeck Creek; N. Dean, Walker Al, Chestnut.

sheet-21-1.description: Part 1 is the upper half of sheet 21, drawn at 100 feet to an inch, with north slightly to the right of straight up. It lies along the northern boundary of Englewood: the top edge is lettered Borough of Bergenfield on the left and Borough of Tenafly on the right, with Ivy Lane and Ivy Avenue along the borough line. Manor Road runs down the middle and Knickerbocker Road down the right edge, crossed by Marlboro Road, Windsor Road, Hudson Avenue, Murray Avenue and Lantata Avenue. Most of the left half is laid out in long narrow lots shown with plan numbers 23A, 23C, 23E, 40A, 40D and 40, with no buildings, while the right half is built up with small frame dwellings along the cross streets (plan numbers 23B, 23D, 23F, 40B and 40C). Several blocks are marked as from plans. Cambridge Avenue is lettered at the right edge near the bottom, where a compass rose and the heavy dividing line of the sheet appear. Six-inch water pipes run in most streets. The lower half of the sheet (part 2) is drawn separately below the heavy line.
notes: Hudson Avenue is West Hudson Avenue in OpenStreetMap; Lantata Avenue is Lantana Avenue (the sheet's spelling is kept in the street list).
Lantana Avenue / Knickerbocker Road was rejected as an outlier by the detector (15 m).
Everett Avenue and Ames were read from the overview lettering and are medium confidence; Everett is Everett Place in OpenStreetMap.

sheet-21-2.description: Part 2 is the lower half of sheet 21, below the heavy dividing line lettered Borough of Tenafly, drawn at 100 feet to an inch. It is turned slightly to the right of the upper half. Along the top runs the borough line with Ivy Lane and Ivy Avenue; Hudson Avenue forms the bottom edge. Knickerbocker Road runs down the left edge, and from it Mountain View Road, Valley View Road and Conrad Road run south to Hudson Avenue as parallel streets with closely built blocks of small frame dwellings (plan numbers 24, 25 and 26). Barling Place, Pleasant Avenue and Vermilye Street lie on the right, where larger lots are marked 5, 6 and 7. The Actors Fund Home stands in grounds at the lower centre-right, and a few houses and a print shop stand on Pleasant Avenue. A compass rose stands at the right edge by Vermilye Street. House numbers and six-inch pipes are marked along the streets. Marlboro Road is lettered near Knickerbocker Road at the left.
notes: Mountain View Road is Mountainview Road, Valley View Road is Valleyview Road, Barling Place is Barling Street and Hudson Avenue is West Hudson Avenue in OpenStreetMap.
This half is drawn out of line with the upper half of the sheet and was placed separately.

sheet-22-1.description: Part 1 is the main map of sheet 22, drawn at 100 feet to an inch and turned about 15 degrees, with north toward the upper left. It shows a strip of Englewood between Tenafly Road on the right edge and Knickerbocker Road on the left, built up with small frame dwellings. Hudson Avenue, Everett Place, Cambridge Avenue and St. Nicholas Avenue run diagonally across the sheet from lower left to upper right, with long narrow lots between them (plan numbers 27, 30, 31 and 43). Central Avenue curves down the middle from St. Nicholas Avenue to Tryon Avenue and Jane Street, with Katherine Street and Alden Place on its west side around a tightly built block (42A and 42). At Tryon Avenue stands the greenhouse works of Peter Duff and Sons, and larger plots and open ground lie to the south. Murray Avenue and Lantata Avenue are lettered at the left edge, where Ames and Knickerbocker Road also appear. A compass rose stands at the top left and the Englewood stamp at the top. A boxed inset of Jane Street (part 2) sits at the lower left, outside this part.
notes: Hudson Avenue is West Hudson Avenue in OpenStreetMap; Lantata Avenue is Lantana Avenue.

Central Avenue, Katherine Street and Alden Place were left out of the control: Central Avenue junctions came out 7 to 8 m from their modern nodes, and Katherine Street 6 m, so the modern lines are displaced from the drawn ones.

sheet-22-2.description: Part 2 is a small boxed inset at the lower left of sheet 22, enclosed by a heavy line and drawn at 100 feet to an inch. It shows Jane Street running across the block from left to right, with a short row of frame dwellings and sheds on the lots on both sides of the street, numbered 208, 206 and 200 on the north side and 49 for the plan block below. Central Avenue is lettered vertically along the right side of the box, with a six-inch water pipe in it, and the inset is marked 37 and 22 for the neighbouring sheets. A north arrow points to the upper left, and six-inch pipes run in Jane Street. The inset repeats a corner that part 1 also draws, but offset from it, so it was placed separately from a single point.

sheet-23-1.description: Part 1 is the upper half of sheet 23, above the heavy dividing line, drawn at 100 feet to an inch and turned with north to the upper left. The top edge follows the Borough Line with Tenafly. Phelps Avenue runs along the top left, with Serpentine Avenue crossing it, and Ivy Avenue and Hudson Avenue run across at the first cross street. Railroad Avenue runs down the left side beside the tracks of the Northern Railroad of New Jersey (Erie), with Cottage Place leading off Hudson Avenue towards Concord, and Engle Avenue runs down the right. The blocks are numbered 2, 3, 14, 15, 16, 17 and 20; houses are small frame dwellings along the street frontages, and a building lettered Northside American Legion Post No. 122 stands near Serpentine Avenue. The lower margin of the part is Brookside Cemetery, with the heavy line below it. The compass rose is at the right and the Englewood stamp at the top right.
notes: Serpentine Avenue is Serpentine Road, Ivy Avenue is East Ivy Lane, Hudson Avenue is East Hudson Avenue and Engle Avenue is Engle Street in OpenStreetMap.

sheet-23-2.description: Part 2 is the lower half of sheet 23, below the heavy dividing line lettered Borough of Tenafly, drawn at 100 feet to an inch and turned with north to the upper left. The top of the part follows the Borough Line, with a row of frame dwellings on Ivy Avenue (plan 1). Railroad Avenue runs down the right side beside the Erie tracks; Orchard and Garden run down the right and centre, and Hudson Avenue crosses on a diagonal from the lower left to the upper right. Tenafly Road runs from the upper left to the bottom, where Highwood Avenue crosses at the lower edge. At the lower left Pleasant Avenue and Vermilye lead off Tenafly Road into a small plan (4, 7). A large open tract (8) holds a church and large houses; the Hudson Gardens apartments and the Reformed Church of Englewood stand on Hudson Avenue, and a group of buildings including an auto shop stands near the railroad. A margin note reads that this territory is now shown on the Map of Tenafly. Everett Place is lettered at the bottom edge.
notes: Hudson Avenue is West Hudson Avenue and Ivy Avenue is West Ivy Lane in OpenStreetMap.
The part fits about 3 percent larger than the other 100 ft sheets (4.09 px/ft against about 3.97); medium confidence.
A margin note reads: This territory now shown on Map of Tenafly.

100 ft. Two parts along the Tenafly line: 1 top (Phelps Av, Ivy Av, Hudson Av, Railroad Av, Cottage Pl, Engle Av, Concord, Brookside Cemetery); 2 bottom (Ivy, Tenafly Rd, Hudson, Garden, Orchard, Highwood Av, Vermilye, Pleasant Av).

sheet-24.description: Sheet 24 covers a residential district in the north of Englewood east of Tenafly Road, drawn at 100 feet to an inch, with the Northern Railroad of New Jersey (Erie) along the right edge. Tenafly Road runs down the left side and is crossed by short streets: Everett, Cambridge, Saint Nicholas, Tryon and Jane. Highwood Avenue crosses the top; Cambridge, Highland and Orchard make a pattern of angled streets in the upper middle, and Durie Avenue and Brook Avenue cross diagonally in the lower half. Roosevelt Square wraps around a block in the lower middle. Valley and Willow are drawn as unbuilt streets in the open ground at the middle right, and Railroad Avenue and Browne run beside the tracks at the lower right, near a street marked Not Named. Overpeck Creek, drawn in blue, passes under the tracks at the middle right and runs south-west. The blocks are houses on narrow lots, with a large tract of long unbuilt lots near the railroad in blocks 13 and 29. The Cleveland School stands on the west side of block 32A, a pink fireproof school with an assembly hall. Block numbers 13, 28, 29, 32A, 32B, 33, 34, 35, 36, 44A, 44B, 44C, 44D and 44E are printed.
notes: St. Nicholas Av. is read here as Saint Nicholas Avenue; it is Saint Nicholas Avenue in OpenStreetMap.
Cambridge Street is Cambridge Avenue in OpenStreetMap; Highland and Orchard are Highland Street and Orchard Street.
Valley, Willow, Railroad Avenue and Browne are not in the OpenStreetMap extract as streets used here.
Highwood Avenue and Orchard Street: the junction measured 12 m from its modern position and was rejected.
Cleveland School stands on the west side of block 32A.
100 ft. Tenafly Rd, Highwood to Brook Av, Erie tracks along the right edge.

sheet-25-1.description: Part 1 of sheet 25 is the left (west) half of the sheet, separated from part 2 by a heavy vertical line, in the north-eastern residential district of Englewood. It is drawn at 100 feet to an inch and turned so that north points to the upper left. Engle runs down the west edge, crossed by Glenwood Road near the top, Booth Avenue below it, Hamilton Avenue and Chestnut near the bottom. King runs north from Chestnut to Hamilton, and Winthrop Place leaves Chestnut at the bottom. Glenwood Road curves in an arc across the upper part, with a brook crossing it and running down through the middle of the part toward Booth Avenue. Most blocks are large lots with frame dwellings and auto houses, many standing well back from the street, and a good deal of land is open. The one large building is the Tudor Apartments, a brick structure on the north side of Booth Avenue near Engle, drawn with fire escapes, standpipes and 2 1/2 inch hose connections. Six-inch water pipes run in Glenwood Road, Booth Avenue, Hamilton Avenue and Chestnut, with 8 and 12 inch mains in Chestnut at the west edge. A dash-dot match line with lettered ends (A and B) crosses the east side of the part; the part is continued on sheet 26 to the east and on sheet 14 to the north. Blocks are numbered 37, 38, 57, 59 and 60, and the adjoining sheets are referred to as 14, 17, 26 and 27.
notes: Hamilton Avenue is East Hamilton Avenue in OpenStreetMap.
King is King Street today; Engle is Engle Street.
The street lettered Browne's Ter. at the west edge is cut off by the sheet edge and was not used for control.
Low confidence on Browne's Terrace: the label is only partly on the part.

100 ft. Two parts split by a heavy vertical line: 1 left (Engle, Glenwood Rd, Booth Av, Hamilton Av, King, Chestnut); 2 right (Engle, Church, Spring La, Hillside Av, Palisade Av; high school, post office).

sheet-25-2.description: Part 2 of sheet 25 is the right (east) half of the sheet, to the east of a heavy vertical line, and shows the centre of Englewood around Engle, drawn at 100 feet to an inch and turned so that north points to the upper left. Chestnut runs across the top with King Street leaving it to the north, and Engle runs down the left side past East (West) Demarest Avenue, Church, Park Place, Spring Lane and Bergen Street to Palisade Avenue and Grand Avenue at the bottom. Winthrop Place curves down the right side to become Hillside Avenue, which runs to Palisade Avenue. Church buildings include St. Paul's Episcopal Church with its rectory and hall, and the First Church of Christ, Scientist. Franklin Public School and Englewood High School, drawn in pink brick with an auditorium and swimming pool, stand between Spring Lane and Palisade Avenue; the Post Office, the Free Public Library and a bank face Palisade Avenue at the foot of the part. The Mayflower Apartments and a group of auto showrooms and repair shops stand along Engle near the top, and a narrow strip of lots between Engle and the heavy line is served by Walker Alley. Water mains of 6, 8, 12 and 24 inches run in Engle, Palisade Avenue and Chestnut. The compass rose sits on the heavy line at the middle of the sheet. Blocks are numbered 73, 74, 114 and 115.
notes: East (West) Demarest Avenue is lettered E.(W.) Demarest St Av.; it is East Demarest Avenue in OpenStreetMap.
Chestnut is Chestnut Street and Church is Church Street; King Street is King Street today.

Winthrop Place continues south as Hillside Avenue; OpenStreetMap shows the two offset by about 60 m at Church Street, so Church Street / Winthrop Place and Church Street / Hillside Avenue were not used as control.
Palisade Avenue is East Palisade Avenue in OpenStreetMap; Walker Alley is probably today's Walkers Lane.

100 ft. Two parts split by a heavy vertical line: 1 left (Engle, Glenwood Rd, Booth Av, Hamilton Av, King, Chestnut); 2 right (Engle, Church, Spring La, Hillside Av, Palisade Av; high school, post office).

sheet-26.description: Sheet 26 shows the north-eastern part of Englewood around Booth Avenue, Lydecker Street and Glenwood Road, at 100 feet to an inch, turned so that north points to the upper left (rotation about 35 degrees). Lydecker runs from the top of the sheet down to Chestnut at the bottom, crossed by Glenwood Road near the top, Booth Avenue near the middle and Hamilton Avenue near the bottom. Glenwood Road bends in an arc, meeting Orient Way and Lydecker at a skew junction at the upper left. Forest Road runs north from Booth Avenue toward Glenwood Road, and Thornton Road, a broad curve, sweeps down the right side to Booth Avenue. Chestnut closes the bottom, ending at Johnson Avenue at the lower right, with Winthrop Place and Hillside Avenue entering it at the lower left. The land is mostly large lots with scattered frame dwellings and auto houses; a stream crosses Booth Avenue near Lydecker and runs east through blocks 57 and 61. Six-inch water pipes run in Booth Avenue, Glenwood Road, Hamilton Avenue and Lydecker, with a twelve-inch main in Chestnut. A fire alarm box stands at Booth Avenue and Lydecker. A dash-dot match line with lettered ends runs near each side edge, joining sheet 25 on the west and sheet 28 on the east; blocks 18B, 20A, 20B, 20C, 37, 38, 39, 57, 60 and 61 are numbered.
notes: Forest Road is Morrow Road in OpenStreetMap; Hamilton Avenue is East Hamilton Avenue.
Orient Way is not in the OpenStreetMap extract.
Booth Avenue / Thornton Road was drawn about 8 m east of the modern junction and was not used as control; Thornton Road is probably realigned.
Lydecker is Lydecker Street, Chestnut is Chestnut Street.
The fitted scale is about 3.5 percent below that of the neighbouring sheets (3.81 px/ft).
100 ft. Glenwood Rd to Chestnut, Lydecker to Johnson Av; Forest Rd = Morrow Road.

sheet-27.description: Sheet 27 covers a residential district on the hillside above central Englewood, between Chestnut Street at the top and Palisade Avenue at the bottom, drawn at 100 feet to an inch and turned so that north lies towards the upper left. Hillside Avenue curves from the top of the sheet down the left side, and Lydecker Street runs diagonally from the top centre to the bottom right. Chestnut, Cedar and Walnut streets cross between them, Church Street and Winthrop Place enter at the left edge, and Spring Lane is a short stub off Hillside Avenue. Chestnut Street bends to the east across the top right towards Johnson Avenue and Brayton Street. The numbered blocks (75 to 79, 116 and 117) hold mostly large frame dwellings with rear auto houses, drawn in yellow, with a few brick and tile houses in pink and stone or concrete ones in blue, standing on wide lots. The Englewood Club occupies a lot on Palisade Avenue at the lower left, with a tennis court and a squash court drawn behind it, and a Conservatory of Music stands in block 117 on the lower right. Several greenhouses and gate houses are scattered among the estates. The large right-hand portion of the sheet, between Lydecker Street and the heavy vertical line at the edge of sheet 29, holds only a few buildings and much open ground. Water pipes of 4, 6, 8 and 12 inches are shown in the streets, with hydrants and fire alarm boxes. The scale bar, the compass rose and the numbers of adjoining sheets (12, 24, 26, 28, 29 and 30) are printed in the margins.
notes: Chestnut, Church, Walnut, Cedar and Lydecker are Chestnut Street, Church Street, Walnut Street, Cedar Street and Lydecker Street in OpenStreetMap.
Palisade Avenue is East Palisade Avenue in OpenStreetMap.
Winthrop Place, Church Street and Walnut Street are drawn some metres off their modern lines and were left out of the georeferencing.
The Englewood Club stands on the north side of Palisade Avenue.
A Conservatory of Music is shown in block 117.
100 ft. Hillside Av, Lydecker, Chestnut, Church, Walnut, Cedar, Palisade Av; Englewood Club.

sheet-28.description: Sheet 28 shows the north-eastern edge of the built-up part of Englewood, drawn at 100 feet to an inch and turned so that north lies towards the upper left. Booth Avenue crosses the top of the sheet from Lincoln Street to Woodland. Lincoln runs down the middle of the sheet as a long, straight street, Brayton runs down the left side, and Woodland runs down the right side. Johnson Avenue comes in diagonally from the top centre and meets Brayton and Chestnut Street at the left edge; a small brook runs alongside it and is drawn in blue. Cedar, Walnut and Pershing Avenue enter from the left and right margins. Most of the sheet is occupied by two very large blocks, 62 between Brayton and Lincoln and 63 between Lincoln and Woodland, which hold only a scattering of estate buildings: dwellings in pink and yellow with outbuildings, greenhouses and garages, and a few stables, set well back from the streets. Block 63 is almost empty except for its edges. The Dwight Junior School, a private school, stands at the lower left near Walnut and Brayton, and a dwelling marked as drawn from plans stands to its east. A dash-dot line near the left edge marks the boundary of the sheet. Water pipes of 6 and 12 inches are shown in Johnson Avenue, Booth Avenue, Lincoln, Brayton and Walnut, together with hydrants, fire alarm boxes and a few telephone poles. Adjoining sheet numbers 20C, 21, 22, 26, 27, 29 and 64A to 64C are printed on the margins.
notes: Lincoln, Woodland, Brayton, Walnut, Cedar and Chestnut are Lincoln Street, North Woodland Street, Brayton Street, Walnut Street, Cedar Street and Chestnut Street in OpenStreetMap.
The left-hand Chestnut is printed Chesnut Street, the right-hand one Chestnut.
The Dwight Junior School stands at the lower left.
Booth Avenue junctions disagree by 5 to 6 m with the rest of the sheet's control, so Booth Avenue was left out of the georeferencing.
100 ft. Booth Av, Lincoln, Woodland, Brayton, Johnson Av, brook; large estates; Dwight Junior School.

sheet-29.description: Sheet 29 lies in the hill district of north-eastern Englewood, drawn at 100 feet to an inch and turned so that north lies towards the upper left. Palisade Avenue crosses the middle of the sheet from left to right. Above it, Brayton and Lincoln run up the sheet as two diverging streets, Lincoln bending in a wide curve, and Walnut crosses the top, bending around the corner of the Brayton block. Woodland runs down the right edge and continues south-east below Palisade Avenue. Below Palisade Avenue, Jones Road runs south-east from the Brayton junction and Beech Road leaves Lincoln at an angle, runs down to an elbow and then follows two sides of a long block to Mountain Road, which crosses the bottom of the sheet. Dana Place enters at the lower left. The Dwight School for Young Ladies occupies the centre of the upper part of the sheet, with a main school building, a gymnasium and dormitories, and the note that it is heated by steam and lit by electricity. The blocks are numbered 117 to 119 above Palisade Avenue and 154 to 157 below it. Most of the buildings are large dwellings of frame or stone with auto houses, greenhouses and sheds on wide lots, drawn in yellow, blue and pink; the left part of block 117 and the large block 155 are sparsely built. A dash-dot line runs down the left margin, and the adjoining sheet numbers 27, 28, 30 and 64 are printed in the margins. Six- and twelve-inch water pipes are shown in all streets, with hydrants and fire alarm boxes. The scale bar and a compass rose showing north to the upper left are drawn on the sheet.
notes: Walnut, Brayton, Lincoln, Woodland and Palisade Avenue are Walnut Street, Brayton Street, Lincoln Street, North and South Woodland Street and East Palisade Avenue in OpenStreetMap.
The Dwight School for Young Ladies is lettered across blocks 118 and 119.
Walnut Street is drawn some metres off its modern line and was left out of the georeferencing; the Lincoln, Beech and Palisade Avenue junction was excluded because it fitted 4 to 5 m off.
100 ft. Palisade Av, Beech Rd, Jones Rd, Mountain Rd, Dana Pl.

sheet-30-1.description: Sheet 30, part 1, is the main map of the sheet and covers a residential district on the ridge east of central Englewood, drawn at 100 feet to an inch and turned so that north lies towards the upper left. Palisade Avenue runs along the top edge, and Dwight Place runs down the left side from Palisade Avenue to Linden Avenue at the bottom, with Dana Place forming the long right-hand side of the district as it runs diagonally from the top centre down to Linden Avenue, where Broad Avenue leads off past a brook drawn in blue. Tracy Place, Lyman Place, Sherwood Place, Chester Place, Maple Avenue and Franklin Avenue cross or enter from Dwight Place in turn, and Mountain Road enters from the right at about the middle of the sheet. Lyman Place ends at the east in a circular turn-around. The blocks are numbered 153 and 154 at the top, 174 and 175 in the middle and 176 and 177 on the right. In the north-west corner stands a large Presbyterian church with a heating and electric-lighting note and an emergency exit, the largest building on the sheet, with a block of attached dwellings drawn in blue behind it. Most of the district is made up of frame dwellings with rear auto houses on regular lots along Sherwood Place and Maple Avenue, with larger properties towards Palisade Avenue and east of Dana Place. A brook crosses the right-hand blocks and runs under Linden Avenue. Six-inch and eight-inch water pipes run in the streets, with hydrants. The heavy-ruled box at the top right is a separate part of the sheet. The numbers of adjoining sheets (12, 13, 27, 29, 33 and 34), the scale bar and the compass rose are printed in the margins.
notes: Palisade Avenue is East Palisade Avenue in OpenStreetMap.
Tracy Place is Tracey Place in OpenStreetMap.
Maple Avenue is Maple Street, Franklin Avenue is Franklin Street and Linden Avenue is East Linden Avenue today.
Sheet 13 prints Chester Place as Chestnut Place.
Dana Place junctions at Palisade Avenue and Mountain Road and the Tracy Place junction fitted 4 to 6 m off the sheet's other control and were excluded from the georeferencing.
The Presbyterian church stands at the north-west corner of the sheet.
100 ft. Two parts: 1 main (Dwight Pl to Dana Pl, Palisade Av to Linden Av); 2 top-right box (Mountain Rd, Jones Rd, Maple Av).

sheet-30-2.description: Sheet 30, part 2, is the box ruled off in heavy black lines at the top right of sheet 30, drawn at 100 feet to an inch and turned like the rest of the sheet so that north lies towards the upper left. It shows a strip of the ridge district east of Dana Place along Jones Road. Mountain Road crosses the top of the box, and Maple Avenue crosses the bottom, with Jones Road running diagonally between them as a 50-foot street, lettered along its length. Beyond Jones Road, at the right, the ground is the numbered block 178 and is blank. The blocks between are numbered 176 and 177. They are divided into narrow lots running up from Maple Avenue, with a few frame dwellings drawn in yellow and a couple in pink, and several auto houses and sheds. Six-inch water pipes and hydrants are marked in Mountain Road and Maple Avenue. The numbers 29 and 30 are printed beside the box to mark the sheets it adjoins. The Englewood date stamp and the sheet number 30 are printed in the upper right corner of the box. The box has no street junction with the main map of sheet 30 and was placed from Jones Road alone.
notes: Maple Avenue is Maple Street in OpenStreetMap.
Placed from two junctions on Jones Road only, as a helmert fit.
100 ft. Two parts: 1 main (Dwight Pl to Dana Pl, Palisade Av to Linden Av); 2 top-right box (Mountain Rd, Jones Rd, Maple Av).

sheet-31.description: Sheet 31 covers the south-western edge of Englewood at 100 feet to an inch, with north towards the upper left. The sheet has two parts. In the upper half, Wilbur runs across the top from Lafayette Avenue on the left to Park Avenue and Elmore Avenue, which run south between lots of small detached dwellings and auto houses. A brook, drawn in blue, crosses the block between Park Avenue and the wedge-shaped Mackay Park, and the broad open area below Wilbur, with a compass rose, junk yard, a large building and some sheds near Lafayette Avenue, is mostly vacant. Overpeck Creek runs from top to bottom down the right-hand side, next to Mackay Park. The lower half is a gridded district of narrow blocks between Lafayette Avenue on the west and Twisby Place on the east, cut by 3rd, 2nd and 1st streets and Warren, with 4th Street running north to south through the middle. Nearly every lot carries a small frame dwelling with an auto house or shed. Institutions include Ebenezer Baptist Church (Colored) on 3rd Street, the Community Center A.M.E. Church (Colored) and a large church building on 2nd Street, the Seventh Day Adventists Church near Warren, a brick garage at the lower left, and a filling station on Lafayette Avenue. Block numbers 132, 135, 137, 165, 181 to 185 and 183A to 183C and the numbers of adjoining sheets (6, 7, 8, 32, 36 and 38) are printed on the sheet. The scale bar and the Sanborn copyright note are at the lower right.
notes: Lafayette Avenue on this sheet is Lafayette Place in OpenStreetMap.
Wilbur and Warren are printed without a suffix; today they are Wilbur Street and Warren Street.
Garden Street / Lafayette Place was detected 7.8 m from the fit and rejected.
Maple Street here may correspond to Hirliman Road in OpenStreetMap; not checked and not used as control.
100 ft. Wilbur, Lafayette Av, Park/Elmore, 1st to 4th streets, Warren, Mackay Park, Overpeck Creek.

sheet-32.description: Sheet 32 covers the south-western district of Englewood, drawn at 100 feet to an inch and turned so that north points to the upper left. Jay crosses the top; William, Humphrey and South Van Brunt run down the sheet from Jay to Linden Avenue and on past Columbus Avenue to Forest Avenue at the bottom. Overpeck Creek flows down the west side from the top, with Mackay Park lettered beside it, and a brook joins it near the lower left. West of the creek at the lower left a separate small district is laid out along First Street, Twisby Place and Epps Avenue, with Warren Street entering Twisby Place. The blocks between Jay and Linden Avenue (numbered 167, 168 and 169) are closely built with frame dwellings on narrow lots, with an A.M.E. Zion church, a plumbing supply store and a large garage drawn in blue. South of Linden Avenue the blocks (262, 263, 264, 188) are almost empty, except for the Englewood Laundry on Columbus Avenue and a grandstand on the west side. The right edge is taken by the Erie railroad with its yards, a freight house, plumbing and heating supply buildings and the City of Englewood garage. Haase Place runs beside the tracks at the foot. Six-inch water pipes run in most streets. The adjoining sheets 8, 9, 11, 31, 33 and 36 are referred to in the margins.
notes: Jay is Jay Street, William is William Street and Humphrey is Humphrey Street in OpenStreetMap; Linden Avenue is West Linden Avenue and Forest Avenue is West Forest Avenue.
School Street is not in the OpenStreetMap extract.
Haase Place is drawn beside the railroad, about 100 m west of the modern street, and was not used for control.
1st Street / William Street is drawn about 12 m from the modern junction and was not used.
100 ft. Jay to Forest Av, Overpeck Creek to the Erie; First St, Twisby Pl, Epps Av district.

sheet-33.description: Sheet 33 shows the district south and east of the Erie railroad in south-western Englewood at 100 feet to an inch, turned so that north points to the upper left. Linden Avenue crosses the top. South Dean runs down the west side from Forest Avenue, past Florence and Grant to Honeck (Bancker), crossed at the foot by Banker (Henry Av.). Grand Avenue is a broad diagonal from the top centre to the lower right, with Mary running parallel to it in the middle of the sheet. East of Grand Avenue, Huguenot Avenue, Starling Road, Audubon Road, Dwight Place, Meadowbrook Road and Madison Avenue make up a grid of large lots. The most conspicuous feature is the group of greenhouses on the T. W. Lydecker Estate, a large block of long glass houses, with a row of blue buildings beside Grand Avenue. At the west edge the Public Service Electric and Gas Company's Englewood Distribution Building, with its fireproof construction, and Burns Bros. coal yard stand beside the railroad, drawn as the N. R. R. of N.J. (Erie) with Haase Place, Lewis Street and Henry Street along it. Filling stations stand on Forest Avenue and Grand Avenue. Houses are mostly frame dwellings on 25 foot lots; blocks 189 to 193, 211A to 211D, 212 to 215 are numbered. Adjoining sheets 11, 13, 30, 32, 34, 35 and 36 are named in the margins.
notes: Linden Avenue is East Linden Avenue, Forest Avenue is East Forest Avenue and Dean is South Dean Street in OpenStreetMap.
Banker (Henry Av.) is Bancker Street today.
Mary Street was left out of the fit: its junctions lay 4 to 9 m east of the modern line while Grand Avenue lay 3 to 7 m west.
Haase Place, Lewis Street and Henry Street are drawn beside the railroad out of position and were not used for control.
Fitted with RMSE of about 3.9 m and a leave-one-out error of 6.9 m; low to medium confidence.
100 ft. Linden Av to Banker (Henry Av), S. Dean to Audubon Rd; Lydecker greenhouses; Haase Pl, Lewis, Henry beside the railroad out of position.

sheet-34.description: Sheet 34 shows a district in the south-east of Englewood around Broad Avenue, at 100 feet to an inch, turned so that north points to the upper left. Linden Avenue runs across the top, with Dana Place leaving it at Broad Avenue. Broad Avenue, an 80 foot street, runs diagonally from the top to the foot with a brook, shown in blue, along its west side. West of it a grid of lots between Huguenot Avenue, Meadowbrook Road and Madison Avenue is cut by Audubon Road and Robin Road; blocks 265 to 268 are narrow lots with frame dwellings. East of Broad Avenue, Hutchinson Road, Arch Road and Fountain Road enclose a rounded block of large estates (195, 196), and Jones Road runs down the right edge from Linden Avenue. Sunset Avenue crosses the lower right and passes the grounds of The Edgewater Creche for Convalescent and Delicate Babies, with its summer and isolation cottage, memorial home and administration cottage, drawn on two private streets. Roosevelt School, a large brick building heated by steam, stands at the foot of the sheet near Madison Avenue and Amy. Six-inch water pipes run in the streets, with larger mains in Broad Avenue and Linden Avenue. The compass rose is at the left. Adjoining sheets 29, 33 and 35 are named in the margins; the dog kennels and a green house stand north of Hutchinson Road.
notes: Linden Avenue is East Linden Avenue, Dana Place is Dana Place in OpenStreetMap.
Broad Avenue was left out of the fit: its modern line lies 8 to 20 m from the drawn one, and Madison Avenue lay about 28 m from the modern line.
Only the Audubon / Robin / Huguenot / Meadowbrook grid on the west side was used for control; the east side is placed by extrapolation, low confidence.
Roosevelt School and the Edgewater Creche are named on the sheet.
100 ft. Linden Av to Madison Av, Audubon Rd to Jones Rd; Broad Av and Madison Av displaced; Edgewater Creche.

sheet-35.description: Sheet 35 shows the southern part of Englewood between Grand Avenue and Broad Avenue, at 100 feet to an inch, turned so that north points to the upper left. Grand Avenue runs down the west side and Broad Avenue down the east side; Van Nostrand Avenue, Walton, Rockwood Place, Phelps Avenue, Lake and Sheffield Avenue cross between them at regular intervals, giving long narrow blocks (215, 216, 219A, 219B, 220, 222) of small frame dwellings, many with auto houses. At the top left Banker (Henry Av.) and May St. enter Grand Avenue, with Amy St. beside the top edge. Lake runs both across the block in the lower part and down its west side. Crystal Lake, a large artificial lake, lies in the lower right below Sheffield Avenue, drained by a brook that runs along the right edge and by a channel leaving at the bottom; a private road of the Englewood Country Club crosses the brook at Sheffield Avenue. A public school, filling stations and Grand Avenue stores stand on the west side. St. John's Episcopal Church stands near Sheffield Avenue and Brookside Avenue at the lower left. The borough limit with Leonia is drawn as a dash-dot line across the foot. Sheets 33, 34, 36 and 217B are named in the margins; water mains of 24 inches run in Grand Avenue and 6 inches in the cross streets.
notes: Banker (Henry Av.) is Bancker Street today; Sheffield Avenue is East Sheffield Avenue.
Walton is Walton Street and Lake is Lake Street in OpenStreetMap.
May Street and Brookside Avenue were not used for control.
Grand Avenue / Phelps Avenue was rejected as an outlier (10 m).
100 ft. Van Nostrand Av to Sheffield Av, Grand Av to Broad Av; Crystal Lake; Leonia line.

sheet-36-1.description: Part 1 of sheet 36 is a boxed block of the south-west district of Englewood west of the Northern Railroad of New Jersey (Erie), drawn at 100 feet to an inch and turned so that north points to the upper left. It shows the blocks between Forest Avenue at the top and Henry Street at the bottom, with Lewis Street across the middle, and from South William Street on the west through South Humphrey and South Van Brunt to Haase Place, which runs beside the railroad at the east edge. A short stub north of Forest Avenue is lettered South Van Brunt Street. The blocks (numbered 201 to 209) are cut into narrow lots of about 25 feet, built up with one- and two-storey frame dwellings, many of them two-family, with rear auto houses, sheds and a few concrete-block garages; a store stands at the corner of Forest Avenue. The streets are drawn narrow, about 25 to 40 feet, except Henry Street. Water pipes of 6 inches run in Forest Avenue, Lewis Street, Henry Street and the cross streets, with hydrants and a fire alarm box at Forest Avenue. The part is enclosed by a heavy line; the rest of sheet 36 shows other districts. Adjoining sheets 32 (west and north) and 33 (east) are referenced in the margins.
notes: Henry is Smith Street in OpenStreetMap (identified by its spacing from Forest Avenue and Lewis Street).
Forest Avenue is West Forest Avenue; South William and South Humphrey are William Street and Humphrey Street today.
Haase Place as drawn runs beside the railroad, about 100 m west of the modern Haase Place; it was not used for control.
Lewis Street and Henry Street no longer reach South William and South Humphrey in OpenStreetMap.
Drawn about 10 percent larger than the 100 ft scale of the rest of the sheet (fitted 4.3 px/ft against 3.9).

100 ft. Four parts separated by heavy lines, from three districts: part 1 boxed block Forest Av/Lewis/Henry (Smith Street) between S. William and Haase Pl (south-west, drawn about 10 percent large); part 2 upper left Green St to Lafayette Av (Lafayette Place), Maple to Genesee Av; part 3 upper right Lafayette Av, Rosemont Pl, Forest Av, Decatur Av; part 4 the rest: Sheffield Av, Brookside Av, Cedar La along the Erie railroad, Bergen Silk Dyeing Corp, Mill Brook.

sheet-36-2.description: Part 2 of sheet 36 is the upper left block of the sheet, a residential area in the west of Englewood near the Teaneck line, drawn at 100 feet to an inch with north towards the upper left. Green Street runs down its west side and Lafayette Avenue down its east side; between them Maple at the top edge, Garden, Franklin Road and Genesee Avenue cross from west to east, and a private road closes the bottom. Reade Street and Orange Street are lettered where they leave the top edge, and a short stub of 3rd Street leaves Lafayette Avenue to the east. The blocks (numbered 160, 164, 180, 270, 271, 272) are only partly built: frame dwellings of one and two storeys with auto houses stand along Garden, Franklin Road and Genesee Avenue, much of the ground is still in large undivided lots, and the west side of Green Street is laid out in narrow lots with few buildings. A garage and show room of cinder block stands on Lafayette Avenue at Genesee Avenue, and a vendor's shop on Franklin Road. Six-inch water pipes are drawn in every street, with hydrants. The part is bounded by heavy lines from the other parts of the sheet; sheet 38 adjoins at the top and sheet 31 to the east.
notes: Lafayette Avenue is Lafayette Place in OpenStreetMap.
Maple along the top edge appears to be Hirliman Road today; its junction was left out of the fit.
The modern blocks widen southwards by about 13 m more than drawn, so residuals of about 4 m remain at the corners.

100 ft. Four parts separated by heavy lines, from three districts: part 1 boxed block Forest Av/Lewis/Henry (Smith Street) between S. sheet-36-3.description: Part 3 of sheet 36 is the upper right block of the sheet, in the west of Englewood south of part 2, drawn at 100 feet to an inch with north towards the upper left. Lafayette Avenue runs down the east side, with short stubs of 2nd Street, 1st Street and Warren Street leaving it to the east; Rosemont Place crosses the part from the west edge to Lafayette Avenue and Forest Avenue crosses below it, with Decatur Avenue leaving Forest Avenue to the south. The blocks (numbered 180, 198, 199 and 273) hold frame dwellings with auto houses along Rosemont Place and Forest Avenue, a row of cinder-block stores on Forest Avenue, a garage of cinder block holding 100 cars beside Lafayette Avenue, a small pump house, and a filling station at the south-east corner of Lafayette and Forest. The upper part of the block is open ground under the sheet title. Six-inch water pipes run in Rosemont Place, Forest Avenue and Lafayette Avenue. A north arrow stands east of Lafayette Avenue. sheet-36-4.description: Part 4 of sheet 36 covers the remainder of the sheet: an industrial strip along the Northern Railroad of New Jersey (Erie) at the south edge of Englewood, drawn at 100 feet to an inch and turned so that north points to the upper left. Sheffield Avenue crosses the railroad near the top, beside the Sheffield Avenue station and an unnamed street running south along the east side of the tracks; Brookside Avenue leaves the railroad to the east further south, and Cedar Lane runs south-west from the crossing past the works of the Bergen Silk Dyeing Corporation, a large group of brick dye houses, finishing rooms and storage buildings with its own pumps and tanks, described in detail. The New Jersey Paper Tube Company stands west of the tracks and the Highwood Coal Company yard with its sidings and bins north of Sheffield Avenue. Mill Brook and a mill pond wind across the bottom of the sheet, with the city limits line drawn along the brook; much of the ground west of Cedar Lane is open. Frame dwellings line Brookside Avenue and Sheffield Avenue east of the railroad. Adjoining sheets 33 and 35 are referenced.

sheet-37-1.description: Part 1 is the main map of sheet 37, covering the north-west residential district of Englewood between Reiss Avenue and West Palisade Avenue, drawn at 100 feet to an inch and turned so that north points to the upper left. Liberty Road crosses the part diagonally from Reiss Avenue to Knickerbocker Road; Morris Avenue, Herzog Place and Levinsohn Place run between Oakland and Cross Street, and Cleveland runs from Liberty Road to West Palisade Avenue, which forms the bottom edge. Knickerbocker Road runs up the east side of the part to the top of the sheet, with John Street and West Demarest Avenue leaving it to the east. A brook crosses the middle of the part in an open valley between the Cross Street blocks and Cleveland. Most blocks (numbered 87 to 94) are laid out in narrow lots, many still vacant, with one- and two-storey frame dwellings, auto houses and a few stores on West Palisade Avenue; the blocks along Knickerbocker Road are built up more densely. At the north end of Knickerbocker Road stands the Home and Hospital for Crippled Children. Six-inch water pipes run in most streets, with a 24-inch main in Liberty Road. The upper left of the sheet is cut off by heavy lines into two further parts drawn out of position. Adjoining sheets 18, 22 and 38 are referenced.

sheet-38.description: Sheet 38 covers the western edge of Englewood along the Teaneck boundary, at 100 feet to an inch, with north towards the upper left. A dash-dot line labelled as the city limits line and lettered Township of Teaneck crosses the sheet from top left to bottom centre; the ground west of it is blank. West Palisade Avenue runs diagonally across the top with long narrow lots on its south side, and Belmont Street, Oakland Street, Cross Street and Cleveland Street come in from the north. Washington Avenue (Place), Shepard Avenue, Howland Avenue and West Englewood Avenue cross the sheet from side to side, with Palisade Place, Oak, Orange, Green, Reade and West Jay running between them. Mattlage Place forms the right-hand side of the upper blocks, and Lafayette Avenue curves down the right-hand edge to Maple at the bottom. Most lots carry a small frame dwelling with an auto house or shed; the western blocks (121 to 125) are sparsely built, with rows of narrow lots on Howland Avenue, and the lower middle blocks (160 and 161) are almost empty. A garage drawn in blue with cinder block walls and a pink hotel stand near the corner of West Englewood Avenue and Lafayette Avenue. A brook with a small branch, drawn in blue, crosses block 126 at the upper right. Six-inch water pipes run in the streets. Block numbers 120 to 129 and 159 to 163 and the numbers of the adjoining sheets (31, 36, 37 and 6) are printed on the sheet. The scale bar and copyright note are at the lower left.
